speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you have a low-grade fever, an itchy rash, and joint pain after taking antibiotics; can you tell me the specific name of the antibiotic you were prescribed and what infection it was meant to treat?

speaker: Patient
text: 8-year-old girl. The patient was brought to the emergency department because of a 2-day history of low-grade fever, itchy rash, and generalized joint pain. The rash initially started in the antecubital and popliteal fossae before spreading to the trunk and distal extremities. One week ago, she was diagnosed with acute sinusitis and started on amoxicillin. She has no history of adverse drug reactions, and her immunizations are up to date.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Amoxicillin-induced Morbilliform Drug Eruption with Arthralgia. The clinical presentation of a rash starting in flexural areas (antecubital and popliteal fossae) and spreading, combined with fever and joint pain one week after initiating amoxicillin for sinusitis, is highly characteristic of this reaction. Given the clear temporal relationship and specific distribution, no further diagnostic testing is required.
